hypothesis: Expose the FM's L2 weight-decay strength as a tunable hparam (currently hardcoded at a near-zero 1e-6) and sweep it upward, since the BPR training curve's post-peak degradation is a textbook under-regularization signature — a stronger L2 penalty should let training run longer before the pairwise objective starts overfitting per-user idiosyncrasies, recovering some of the primary lost between epoch 6 and the early-stop point.
reflection: BPR (iter 4) worked as predicted — GAUC gained 3x more than nDCG@5, confirming the pairwise objective targets GAUC's own definition — but the training curve shows a clear overfitting signature (peak at epoch 6, degraded by epoch 10), meaning the current L2 (hardcoded at 1e-6, effectively negligible) isn't restraining the pairwise objective from over-fitting user-specific noise as training continues.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since BPR's pairwise loss (and its overfitting) is concentrated on per-user ranking noise exactly like GAUC measures, whereas nDCG@5 already showed a smaller BPR-driven swing last iteration.
